intro: Massage therapy builds hands-on patient care and an eye for how bodies move. The closest of the 25 careers below are Physical Therapist Assistants and Occupational Therapy Assistants, both at an 85% skill match; therapy assistants earn a BLS May 2025 median of $72,300, which is 24% more than massage therapists earn.
why_it_works: Each session you assess tension, adjust pressure and explain care to clients who come back for months. O*NET rates social perceptiveness and service orientation at 3.12 out of 5 for this job. Rehabilitation, recreational therapy and nursing roles rely on the same care. Several need an associate degree or more. The skills to grow are coordination, teaching patients and monitoring their progress.
tips: Look at physical therapist assistant programs; most take about two years and lead to a $68,380 median.
Track your client results and rebooking rate; they show the patient follow-through that clinics want.
If you are ready for longer study, Physical Therapists earn $102,760, or 76% more, with a graduate degree.

faq.q: What jobs can former massage therapists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Physical Therapist Assistants (85%), Occupational Therapy Assistants (85%) and Recreational Therapists (80%), based on O*NET 31.0. Licensed practical nurses are also 79% matched and earn $64,400, which is 10% more than the $58,450 massage therapist median.

faq.q: Which careers for massage therapists pay more?
faq.a: 14 of the 25 matches pay more than massage therapy. Physical Therapists earn $102,760 (76% more), Occupational Therapists $100,330 (72% more) and Registered Nurses $97,550 (67% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. All three need a degree you may not have yet.

faq.q: Do massage therapists need more education to switch?
faq.a: Often yes for the best-paid paths. 13 of the 25 matches need no more education, but 4 usually need a graduate degree. Therapy assistant jobs usually need an associate degree, held by 84% of workers in the closest match, which most programs cover in about two years.

faq.q: What skills should massage therapists learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations monitoring, coordination, instructing and operation and control. Judgment already rates 3 out of 5 for massage therapists in O*NET, so clinical training and teaching patients exercises are the next steps.
